How sure can we be?: Not very sure, so treat this with care. Most of the new water (100%) is on farmland. Radar can't tell a flood from flooded rice fields, and on one farmland test our map and the other satellite's map disagreed almost completely.
What could be wrong?: These are estimates. Very wet fields can sometimes look like water. Some spots, like steep hillsides, can't be seen clearly and are left out. Some NISAR data used is Provisional/Unknown quality; numbers may change when reprocessed. Pass 2026-08-19 is 1.7 dB darker than the others, likely wind, rain or wet soil, so open water may be missed on that date. Pass 2026-09-24 is 2.1 dB brighter than the others, likely wind, rain or wet soil, so open water may be missed on that date. Most detected new water lies on cropland, where radar cannot separate a flood from irrigated or flooded paddies; on one cropland window our map and OPERA disagreed almost completely. This place and these dates have not been compared with OPERA: the method was compared on one lake window (Jul to Oct 2026, track 83) only.
Did the water go down anywhere?: Yes, about 104 hectares dried out, while 285 hectares went under water.
